PullRequest.Title: agentHost: count jobs behind required checks and surface SSO blocks
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Agent Merge sometimes didn't kick in on pull requests with failing CI or merge conflicts. This fixes two causes:

- **Failures behind required checks were ignored.** Only checks GitHub reports as required counted. On microsoft/vscode the aggregate `PR Gate` check is only created once every job it `needs:` has finished, so a failed job went unrepaired for about 20 minutes. The Agents window, the title bar and the PR artifact integration also each judged different checks.
- **Single sign-on blocks were silent.** When GitHub refused the credential for an organization's SAML single sign-on, the pull request lookup only logged a warning. Agent Merge then waited forever while the title bar showed it as on.

## Which checks count

- The pull request query reads the base branch's required checks from branch protection and rulesets, and the `needs:` graph of the workflows that report them, read at the head commit and cached. It marks the checks that each unfinished required check waits for ([`pullRequestRequiredChecks.ts`](src/vs/platform/github/common/pullRequestRequiredChecks.ts)).
- One classifier decides everywhere:
  - Required checks count, plus the checks an unfinished required check waits for.
  - Once a required check finishes, its own result decides.
  - A required check that hasn't reported is pending.
  - If the base branch requires nothing, every check counts.
- The surfaces that use it:
  - Agent Merge: repairing, waiting and merging.
  - The PR artifact integration: Fix CI, the orange PR icon, Mark Ready and Merge.
  - The agent host's title-bar readiness.
  - The Agents window: CI state, Fix CI banner, Fix Checks and blocked sessions. Its CI state shows as loading until the shared pull request data has been read.
  - The workbench GitHub pills.
- `chat.artifactIntegrations.githubPullRequests.autoMarkReadyIgnoredChecks` now also applies to Agent Merge's ready-for-review check. Each folder uses its workspace value.
- Agent Merge also:
  - Keeps a deferred workflow rerun when the gate that waits for the deferred jobs reports its failure.
  - Repairs a check suite that failed without reporting a check run, such as a workflow that failed to start. `readAgentMergeCI` explains that such a suite has no logs.
- Checks are polled sooner while a required check hasn't reported. The Agents window re-reads which checks count when reruns change the reported checks.

## Single sign-on

- The GitHub transport keeps the page GitHub names in `X-GitHub-SSO: required; url=…`. It accepts only a secure `/orgs/<org>/sso` page on the GitHub host the request went to. The page is carried through PR data errors and errors passed between processes.
- `attachSessionGitHubPullRequest` now returns why a pull request lookup failed.
- Agent Merge posts a new `AgentMergeBlocked` notice in two cases:
  - Single sign-on blocks finding or reading its pull request. The notice says "… [Sign in to <org>](…) to authorize it …". GitHub's link expires after an hour, so a fresh notice follows only if Agent Merge is still blocked then.
  - No pull request turns up for its branch within 5 minutes.
- For the PR artifact integration, the `authenticationRequired` state carries the page as `authorizationUrl`, and **Sign In** opens it instead of signing in again.

## Notes for reviewers

- Behavior changes:
  - When the base branch requires checks, a failing optional check no longer shows Fix CI or the orange PR icon.
  - A missing required check blocks merging and Mark Ready.
  - The overall status shows failure as soon as one counted check fails.
  - A cancelled check counts as failed.
- Workflows are read at the PR head, not the merge commit. YAML anchors aren't supported, so jobs after an anchor contribute no dependencies.
- GitHub authorizes each token for single sign-on separately. The link authorizes exactly the token Agent Merge used, which the Agents window GitHub features share.

## How to test

Validation run on this commit:

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `npm run eslint -- <the 51 changed TypeScript files>`: passed
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --runGlob "**/{platform/github,platform/agentHost,platform/artifactIntegrations,sessions/contrib,sessions/services,workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions,workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentHost,workbench/contrib/github,workbench/services/github}/**/*.test.js"`: passed, 28,990 passing and 100 pending

Checked by hand during development:
- Ran the real GitHub client, query and gate code against live microsoft/vscode PRs. With `PR Gate` not yet reported, #344458 got a Fix CI repair for `Copilot - Test (Linux)` and `Copilot - Test (Windows)`, and #344461 for `Windows / Electron-Smoke (shard 2/3)`.
- For the conflicting PRs #340701 and #344545, Agent Merge prompts only `resolveConflicts`. GitHub Actions doesn't run on a conflicting head, so its required checks stay pending.

Manual steps:
1. Turn on Agent Merge for a PR whose `PR Gate` jobs fail before `PR Gate` reports. A Fix CI repair starts for the failed job, and the Agents window's Fix CI banner lists that job.
2. Use a GitHub sign-in that isn't authorized for an organization's single sign-on, and turn on Agent Merge for a PR there. A warning notice with **Sign in to <org>** appears. After you authorize through the link, Agent Merge continues within a minute.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The two independent schedulers, their 60-second pending intervals, the unchanged REST fetch, the new GraphQL call path, and the all-open-PR consumer are directly traced. Exact latency depends on session count and GitHub response time, but request multiplication is deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For every distinct open pull request retained by the sessions UI, the existing 60-second REST check-runs poll continues while the new shared resource independently polls required checks every 60 seconds while pending (and every 5 minutes otherwise); cost therefore grows linearly with open PR sessions.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased network traffic, GitHub quota consumption, queued-request latency, and slower CI-status updates under many sessions.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: GitHubPullRequestCIModel refreshed check runs through one coalesced model request and one 60-second RunOnceScheduler loop.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each refresh now creates a PullRequestChecksSource subscription. PullRequestResourceService automatically polls that subscription in addition to the unchanged GitHubPullRequestCIModel poller, while the model still calls GitHubPRCIFetcher.getCheckRuns on every legacy cycle.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added call at line 187 starts _subscribeRequiredChecks from refresh without removing the existing _poll/_refresh path; the new source subscribes with required checks, and line 266 also explicitly refreshes it.
Findings.Title: Use one polling loop for each pull request's checks
Findings.Impact: Opening or retaining many sessions with open PRs causes every pending PR to issue roughly the legacy REST poll plus two new GraphQL reads per minute, before cold metadata reads. This can consume GitHub quotas and delay visible CI state as requests queue.
Findings.Evidence: GitHubPullRequestCIModel._refresh still calls GitHubPRCIFetcher.getCheckRuns (one REST check-runs traversal). The added PullRequestChecksSource uses PullRequestResourceService, whose background pending-check policy is 60 seconds and whose required-check fetch performs a GraphQL rollup plus a separate expected-suite GraphQL request, with cold branch/ruleset and workflow reads. github.contribution starts the legacy CI poller for every open non-draft session PR, so the two loops are simultaneously reachable and the request queue only bounds concurrency, not total requests.
Findings.Recommendation: Make the CI model use a single authoritative polling source: either populate its check list/status from PullRequestChecks and remove the legacy getCheckRuns poller, or make the shared subscription passive and refresh it from the existing loop. Keep annotation/output reads on demand.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The cache-write, swallowed-error, and polling paths are explicit. Transport concurrency limits cap simultaneous requests, but neither they nor ETags suppress later retries; prevalence of partial authorization failures affects severity, not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub REST requests for branch protection and rulesets
Findings.PerformanceScaling: After an initial metadata failure, every checks poll for every distinct active PR retries the same base-branch request; pending or missing required checks poll every 15 seconds when visible or 60 seconds in background, and timers for separate PR resources are not request-count coalesced once their calls no longer overlap.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated network I/O, GitHub rate-limit consumption, and request-queue pressure while authorization, SSO, enterprise compatibility, or network failures persist.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Checks polling did not read branch protection or branch rulesets, so these failure retries did not exist.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Required-check refreshes now call _fetchRequiredContexts. Only successful reads populate the five-minute cache; a GitHubRequestError is swallowed by returning cached?.contexts, leaving an initial failure uncached and making the outer resource treat the refresh as successful rather than applying failure backoff.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added return at line 483 exits the failure path without recording a cache state or propagating the error; the added call at line 425 invokes this path on every required-check fetch.
Findings.Title: Back off failed required-context reads
Findings.Impact: A credential that can read PR checks but is blocked from branch/rules metadata—such as an organization SSO or authorization restriction—causes the same failed metadata call to repeat for the lifetime of each active PR, increasing quota pressure and delaying other GitHub work.
Findings.Evidence: _fetchRequiredContexts checks _requiredContexts, performs GET branches/<base> and then GET rules/branches/<base>, and writes the cache only after both succeed. Its catch returns undefined when there was no prior success. PullRequestResourceService therefore commits the checks result and schedules its normal pending cadence rather than _scheduleAfterFailure; missing required checks specifically remain on the fast cadence.
Findings.Recommendation: Store a bounded negative/backoff state per host/repository/base branch (and coalesce an in-flight read), or propagate transient failures so PullRequestResourceService applies its existing exponential backoff. Invalidate terminal authorization negatives when credentials change and retain the last successful contexts while retrying at a bounded interval.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents window, blocked-session rows, title icons, and active-session banners read CI for open pull requests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A CI model first fetches legacy check runs and now also waits for the shared PullRequestChecks subscription before required-check status leaves Loading; both paths are on the visible status/Fix Checks critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List all check runs for the head through the legacy REST client
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One paginated traversal per distinct open PR every 60 seconds while polling; up to 100 pages in extreme cases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This was the single CI checks polling source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Populates the existing checks list used by CI details and triggers status refresh work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read PR core, GraphQL check rollup, expected check suites, required branch/rules contexts, and unfinished-gate workflow files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Warm pending path adds one rollup query and one expected-suite query per PR per minute, plus core every five minutes; cold path adds branch and rules REST reads and at most one batched workflow query for uncached workflow paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The legacy client CI model did not subscribe to this independently polling resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required-check status remains Loading until this path produces current-head data.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct open PR heads represented by retained sessions; checks and suites paginate in groups of 100, while required-context calls group by repository/base branch only when their requests overlap or a successful TTL cache is warm.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each CI model has its existing 60-second poller, while PullRequestResourceService independently polls pending checks every 60 seconds in background. The GitHub RequestQueue limits active work to 12 globally, 10 per account, and 8 per caller, but queued request count and quota usage still scale per PR. Same-PR resource subscriptions and identical in-flight transport requests coalesce.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Pull-request resources share one entry per PR and remain dormant for 120 seconds. Required contexts cache successful values for five minutes; workflow files cache up to 50 commit/path entries. Failed required-context reads have no negative cache. REST ETags reduce response bytes but still consume requests.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both schedulers, request paths, intervals, and all-open-PR consumer are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact user-visible delay depends on retained session count, pagination, and GitHub latency; request multiplication is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated network work: the PR adds a second independent CI polling source without removing the first.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Merge and pull-request artifact automation classify required checks and dependencies
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Checks, expected suites, base-branch requirements, and unfinished-gate workflow definitions must be read before repair, Mark Ready, or merge decisions can progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read branch protection and effective branch rules
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two sequential REST traversals per repository/base branch cache miss; after an initial failure, one or both repeat on every PR checks poll.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Required-check subscriptions only used GitHub-reported requiredness and expected suites; they did not call these REST endpoints.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines missing required checks; failures fall back to per-check requiredness but still complete the outer fetch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read workflow blobs and parse YAML to resolve transitive needs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One GraphQL request containing all uncached workflow paths while required gates are unfinished, normally once per head; failed reads are retried on later polls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No workflow files were fetched on the checks path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Needed to surface failed jobs before an aggregate required gate reports.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read check rollup and expected suites
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least two GraphQL reads per poll before pagination for required-check subscribers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The rollup and expected-suite reads already existed for required-check automation, though the queried metadata is richer now.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Active Agent Merge/artifact PRs, required checks, check pages, distinct workflow paths on each head, and duration for which an aggregate required gate has not reported.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Shared resources coalesce subscribers for the same PR. Distinct PR entries poll independently, with transport admission capped at 12 global/10 account/8 caller requests. Workflow paths are fetched in one GraphQL query per uncached head/path set rather than one request per path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful required contexts live five minutes; workflow parse results are immutable per head/path and capped at 50. Required-context failures are swallowed without a negative entry, so normal 15-second visible or 60-second background pending cadence retries them instead of resource failure backoff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: cache writes, catch behavior, and resource polling cadence are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Partial authorization and enterprise endpoint failures vary by account; when they occur, retry multiplicity is fixed by polling lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cache-lifecycle regression for uncached required-context failures; successful cold metadata fan-out is bounded and justified by the feature.

Scenarios.Scenario: PR links, hover details, pills, and resource details show only counted CI status
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Interactive hover/detail refreshes now request required-check metadata before presenting authoritative status; link and pill watchers otherwise render from shared snapshots off the direct render/layout path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh core and required checks for interactive PR presentation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared resource per distinct PR; cold required status reaches rollup, expected suites, branch/rules, and possibly workflow reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These surfaces requested optional check rollups without branch/rules/workflow dependency classification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Interactive details await checks refresh; passive link watchers update asynchronously.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously visible distinct PR links/pills and number of checks/workflows per PR.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Subscriptions for one PR merge interests into one resource; exact in-flight GitHub reads coalesce, while distinct PRs share the bounded request queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm PR snapshots, five-minute successful required-context entries, and per-head workflow entries reduce repeated cold work. There is no negative required-context cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added request path and sharing behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical simultaneous hover cardinality is low and shared snapshots may already be warm.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: outside the reported failed-cache behavior, the richer cold read is bounded, shared, and required for the changed status semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Merge reports SSO blocks or a branch with no pull request
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Agent Merge's existing evaluation/backstop lookup must finish before it can bind a PR; the new code only carries failure metadata and posts a notice.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Look up the pull request for the current branch
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing sequenced lookup cadence per enabled folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The lookup already occurred and logged failures; the diff returns the failure details to the controller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Agent Merge cannot monitor until lookup succeeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once after five minutes for a missing PR, or once per hour while the same organization remains SSO-blocked.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the progress critical path; user notification only.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled Agent Merge folders and time spent blocked; notices are one per missing PR and at most one per organization per hour for SSO.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pull-request lookups remain sequenced per session/folder by the existing keyed sequencer; Agent Merge backstop cadence remains one minute.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The runtime retains one timestamped SSO notice and one missing-PR waiting record per active folder; both are bounded by runtime lifetime.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; rates are explicitly bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: the added state and IPC notifications are bounded and do not add lookup frequency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workspace ignored-check setting synchronization updates Agent Merge folder state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration changes asynchronously synchronize enabled folders; ordinary CI evaluation does not wait on this loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch updated Agent Merge client state to the host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one write per distinct enabled folder whose effective workspace value changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No workspace ignored-check value was mirrored for Agent Merge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the routine UI and CI critical paths; only configuration propagation waits.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cached sessions, chats, and distinct Agent Merge folders at the moment the setting changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The implementation walks sessions/folders sequentially and awaits each state write, avoiding an IPC burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Folder keys deduplicate multiple chats, structural equality skips unchanged values, and synchronization occurs only on setting/state changes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users with unusually many cached sessions may make a setting change take longer, but changes are rare and writes are deduplicated.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: the boundary work is rare, deduplicated, and serialized.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 53 changed files and relevant callers/tests. Submitted two findings: duplicate per-PR CI polling and missing negative/backoff caching for required-context failures. Other added workflow, SSO, presentation, and configuration paths are bounded or intentionally shared.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
